gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 240 V load (central AC, which Anker names on its F3800 pages) can only run from a battery with a 120/240 V split-phase outlet. Anker's own spec sheet shows even a 6,000 W unit gives 240 V only through its NEMA L14-30R (25 A, 6,000 W max) and caps each 120 V outlet at 20 A / 2,400 W. The 240 V output also can't be used while the unit charges from 120 V AC.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results, so there are no rival pages to compare. Its own answer explains kW vs kWh and has a 'Whole house, including AC: 20–40+ kWh' row. It treats the whole thing as a capacity question and never says that whole-house and AC backup depend on output voltage (120 V only vs 120/240 V split phase) and on a transfer switch or panel, rather than on kWh.
decides: For the shopper's 'whole house including AC' tier, adding kWh is not enough. The unit has to have a 120/240 V L14-30-type output and a transfer switch or home panel, which rules out 120 V-only power stations no matter their capacity. For fridge, Wi-Fi and lights, a 120 V unit is fine and kWh is the right measure. On the pages I opened, the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus is the listed product confirmed to have this output. Its page showed 'Sold Out' with no price on 2026-11-14.
